sun.name: Sun

reference.title: SDO HMI continuum intensity, 21 September 2026
reference.credit: NASA/SDO and the HMI science team
reference.band: HMI continuum intensity near 617.3 nm; grayscale display

features: Observed sunspots and darkening toward the apparent limb
sun.finding: White is appropriate in visible light, but the previous shader had no observed surface detail. Orange and gold solar displays use assigned colours.
sun.action: Project the dated grayscale HMI observation onto its observed hemisphere, remove baked radial shading and apply observer-dependent limb shading. Enable close inspection.
sun.limitations: A single-band browse image is not a calibrated RGB or radiance map. Display exposure and limb law are modelled; orientation is schematic. The unobserved hemisphere and cropped outer limb remain smooth; activity is historical.

references.title: NASA explanation of solar image colours

mercury.name: Mercury

reference.title: Mercury’s True Color is in the Eye of the Beholder
reference.credit: NASA / Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory / Arizona State University / Carnegie Institution of Washington
reference.band: 430 nm grayscale and 480/560/630 nm colour composites, displayed with several stretches

features: Muted grey-brown surface and brighter rays
mercury.finding: The existing map reproduces the cratered, near-grey surface class. The comparison panels demonstrate that processing strongly changes apparent colour.
mercury.action: Retain the official map and restrained surface palette.
mercury.limitations: The visualization map is not radiometrically calibrated. Different contrast stretches in the reference are not different physical surface colours.
mercury.validation: NASA reference photograph, source map and four rendered longitude views inspected. Comparison assesses recognizable morphology and colour class, not photometric equivalence.

venus.name: Venus

reference.title: Venus from Mariner 10
reference.credit: NASA / JPL-Caltech; processing by Kevin M. Gill
reference.band: Orange and ultraviolet filters with synthesized green; false-colour composite

features: Subtle cloud markings; no visible rocky surface
venus.finding: The previous yellow, high-contrast bands overstated the cloud contrast compared with the ordinary-contrast NASA view.
venus.action: Reduce cloud contrast to 15 percent and use a pale cream display tone while retaining the source pattern.
venus.limitations: This is a representative display correction, not calibrated natural colour or current weather. Mariner 10 did not acquire a complete visible RGB set.
venus.validation: NASA reference photograph, source map and four rendered longitude views inspected. Comparison assesses recognizable morphology and colour class, not photometric equivalence.

earth.name: Earth

reference.title: NASA Captures EPIC Earth Image
reference.band: Red, green and blue filtered exposures

features: Blue oceans and continental land patterns
Bright white clouds and polar ice
earth.finding: Blue Marble land/ocean geography and a separate archived cloud map reproduce the observed visual components.
earth.action: Retain the observed surface mosaic and separate cloud layer.
earth.limitations: The surface and cloud composites combine different dates. Cloud opacity and atmosphere are display models, not a reconstruction of the comparison image’s weather.
earth.validation: NASA reference photograph, source map and four rendered longitude views inspected. Comparison assesses recognizable morphology and colour class, not photometric equivalence.

mars.name: Mars

reference.title: Global Color Views of Mars
reference.band: Viking red and violet mosaics with synthesized green

features: Dark regional markings and polar caps
mars.finding: The map preserves dark albedo regions, polar ice and the characteristic dust colour.
mars.action: Retain the NASA map and directional solar illumination.
mars.limitations: The comparison is a processed global composite with contrast adjustments and some interpolated coverage; it is not an instantaneous calibrated RGB observation.
mars.validation: NASA reference photograph, source map and four rendered longitude views inspected. Comparison assesses recognizable morphology and colour class, not photometric equivalence.

jupiter.name: Jupiter

reference.title: Cassini Jupiter Portrait
reference.band: Red, green and blue filtered mosaic

features: Alternating light zones and brown belts
Great Red Spot and smaller atmospheric vortices
jupiter.finding: The Cassini-based cylindrical map preserves the major belts and observed storms in all longitude views.
jupiter.limitations: The map dates to December 2000 and differs in time from the reference portrait. Atmospheric features evolve; neither is current weather.
jupiter.validation: NASA reference photograph, source map and four rendered longitude views inspected. Comparison assesses recognizable morphology and colour class, not photometric equivalence.

saturn.name: Saturn

reference.title: The Greatest Saturn Portrait ... Yet
reference.band: True-colour red, green and blue filtered mosaic

features: Oblate globe with subtle atmospheric bands
Ring divisions, thin outer ring and mutual shadows
saturn.finding: The radial ring texture preserves the principal divisions. Analytic lighting supplies planet-on-ring and ring-on-planet shadows.
saturn.action: Retain the registered ring texture, measured radii and directional shadows.
saturn.limitations: Atmospheric hue varies with season; the map does not recreate the 2004 illumination. Ring alpha is a display quantity rather than measured optical depth.
saturn.validation: NASA reference photograph, source map and four rendered longitude views inspected. Comparison assesses recognizable morphology and colour class, not photometric equivalence.

uranus.name: Uranus

reference.title: Uranus: True and False Color
reference.band: Left: blue/green/orange approximately visible; right: strongly enhanced ultraviolet/violet/orange

features: No bright false-colour polar patch in ordinary visible light
uranus.finding: The restrained cyan atmosphere is consistent with the left, approximately visible-colour image.
uranus.action: Retain the muted cloud appearance and faint rings.
uranus.limitations: The false-colour panel is not used as a natural-colour target. Cloud detail and ring brightness remain illustrative rather than calibrated.
uranus.validation: NASA reference photograph, source map and four rendered longitude views inspected. Comparison assesses recognizable morphology and colour class, not photometric equivalence.

neptune.name: Neptune

reference.title: Neptune Full Disk View
reference.band: Voyager green/orange composite with processed display colour

features: Cloud bands and bright companions to historical dark storms
Pale blue-green visible colour after later reassessment
neptune.finding: The source map preserves Voyager-era cloud morphology. Its intense blue was already reduced to a representative pale blue-green consistent with NASA’s revised description.
neptune.action: Retain the pale display correction and historical cloud map.
neptune.limitations: This is not a new spectrophotometric reconstruction. The 1989 Great Dark Spot is historical; the enhanced blue archive image is not a literal natural-colour target.
neptune.validation: NASA reference photograph, source map and four rendered longitude views inspected. Comparison assesses recognizable morphology and colour class, not photometric equivalence.

references.title: NASA Neptune facts: revised colour and historical storms

moon.name: Moon
features: Dark basaltic maria against brighter highlands
Impact craters and bright ejecta rays
moon.finding: The LROC mosaic preserves the near-side maria and the densely cratered far side in the four longitude views. Separate LOLA elevation data supplies physical-scale surface-normal shading, instead of treating dark maria as depressions.
moon.action: Retain the NASA LROC/LOLA products and the physical elevation scale.
moon.limitations: The colour mosaic is adjusted for visual presentation, with lower-resolution monochrome polar fill and small repaired dropouts. Relief affects shading, not the ellipsoidal silhouette; lighting and rotational phase are schematic.

reference.title: CGI Moon Kit
reference.credit: NASA SVS; LRO/LROC and LOLA teams
reference.band: LROC WAC visible composite; exposure and white balance adapted for display

moon.validation: Official archive image, source map and four rendered longitude views inspected; comparisons assess recognizable structure and colour class, not photometric equivalence.

phobos.name: Phobos
phobos.finding: The native NASA mesh and its original UV atlas retain the irregular outline and resolved crater structure. The renderer uses a dark, nearly neutral surface rather than interpreting the enhanced red/infrared reference as naked-eye colour.
phobos.action: Keep the native mesh, original texture coordinates and diffuse, nonmetallic material.
phobos.limitations: The NASA visualization mesh is not a certified terrain model. Some source lighting remains baked into the texture. The reference uses enhanced colour and does not establish absolute reflectance.

reference.title: Martian Moon Phobos
reference.band: HiRISE blue-green, red and near-infrared; enhanced colour

phobos.validation: Official archive image, source map and four rendered longitude views inspected; comparisons assess recognizable structure and colour class, not photometric equivalence.

io.name: Io
io.finding: The rendered longitude views show the observed mottled pale-yellow surface and dark volcanic features. The surface is illuminated by the Sun rather than glowing orange.
io.action: Retain the spacecraft-derived map and restrained diffuse shading.
io.limitations: The Galileo reference approximates human-visible colour using filters extending into near-infrared. Volcanic deposits change with time; the model is not a current activity map or a reflectance calibration.

reference.title: Global image of Io (true color)
reference.band: Galileo near-infrared, green and violet; approximately human-visible colours

io.validation: Official archive image, source map and four rendered longitude views inspected; comparisons assess recognizable structure and colour class, not photometric equivalence.

europa.name: Europa
europa.finding: The model preserves the dark fracture network on pale ice. Its muted colour is compared with the approximate-natural-colour left panel, not the strongly enhanced right panel.
europa.action: Keep the mapped fractures and neutral ice appearance; do not import false-colour blues or oranges as natural surface colour.
europa.limitations: The source is a global visualization mosaic, not a dated complete observation. Fine fracture relief and subsurface structures are not represented in geometry.

reference.title: Natural and False Color Views of Europa
reference.band: Left: approximate natural colour; right: false-colour violet/green/infrared

europa.validation: Official archive image, source map and four rendered longitude views inspected; comparisons assess recognizable structure and colour class, not photometric equivalence.

ganymede.name: Ganymede
ganymede.finding: The four rendered longitudes preserve the contrast between dark blocks, brighter grooved regions and ray craters seen in Galileo images.
ganymede.action: Retain the observed terrain pattern and subdued brown-grey colour.
ganymede.limitations: Brightness depends on display lighting and exposure; it is not calibrated against this single Galileo frame. The reference ellipsoid does not reproduce local relief.

reference.title: Ganymede Color Global
reference.band: Galileo natural-colour composite

ganymede.validation: Official archive image, source map and four rendered longitude views inspected; comparisons assess recognizable structure and colour class, not photometric equivalence.

callisto.name: Callisto
callisto.finding: Rendered views retain the dense bright-crater pattern against a much darker background. Surface colour is somewhat warmer than the reference image, without changing the recognizable geography.
callisto.action: Retain the source map; avoid an unsupported colour correction from one differently processed hemisphere.
callisto.limitations: The archive reference covers one observed hemisphere, not every longitude. The educational map is not a calibrated spectral-reflectance product, and crater relief is not separately resolved.

reference.title: Global Callisto in Color
reference.band: Galileo global colour observation; not a complete all-longitude map

callisto.validation: Official archive image, source map and four rendered longitude views inspected; comparisons assess recognizable structure and colour class, not photometric equivalence.

mimas.name: Mimas
features: Herschel impact basin with central structure
mimas.finding: The native NASA mesh preserves a cratered irregular surface and the original UV atlas. Herschel is not face-on in every catalogue phase; its position changes with the viewing angle rather than following the camera.
mimas.action: Keep the native geometry and neutral visible appearance. Compare the basin with the monochrome archive mosaic, not the blue-green enhanced-colour image.
mimas.limitations: The educational mesh is not a calibrated Cassini terrain product. Baked source shadows and limited mesh resolution prevent exact reproduction of Herschel under arbitrary illumination.

reference.title: Examining Herschel Crater
reference.band: Cassini visible-light monochrome mosaic

references.title: Color Near Herschel Crater
references.band: Clear-filter detail plus ultraviolet, green and infrared; false colour

mimas.validation: Official archive image, source map and four rendered longitude views inspected; comparisons assess recognizable structure and colour class, not photometric equivalence.

enceladus.name: Enceladus
enceladus.finding: The mapped fracture pattern is retained, but at the shared scene exposure Enceladus appears greyer than its bright natural-colour reference. The prominent blue fractures in the detailed archive composite are enhanced colour, not a natural blue surface.
enceladus.action: Keep geographic detail and record the unresolved absolute-brightness limitation; do not calibrate reflectance from differently exposed photographs.
enceladus.limitations: The source visualization texture is not calibrated relative to other moons. Plumes, small-scale relief and time-dependent activity are not modelled; the UV/infrared reference is used only for terrain-pattern comparison.

reference.title: Fresh Features on Enceladus (False color)
reference.band: Cassini ultraviolet, green and infrared; enhanced colour, blue fractures not natural visible colour

references.title: A Tale of Two Moons
references.band: Cassini red, green and blue natural-colour comparison of Enceladus and Titan

enceladus.validation: Official archive image, source map and four rendered longitude views inspected; comparisons assess recognizable structure and colour class, not photometric equivalence.

tethys.name: Tethys
tethys.finding: The rendered views preserve the predominantly neutral cratered surface, darker equatorial region and large impact features rather than assigning strong false colours.
tethys.action: Retain the mapped surface and compare its broad terrain pattern with Cassini natural-colour imagery.
tethys.limitations: Source-image shading remains in the albedo texture. Small crater relief is not in the reference-ellipsoid geometry, and brightness is not photometrically calibrated.

reference.title: Battered and Grooved
reference.band: Cassini red, green and blue natural-colour mosaic

tethys.validation: Official archive image, source map and four rendered longitude views inspected; comparisons assess recognizable structure and colour class, not photometric equivalence.

dione.name: Dione
dione.finding: The bright branching wisps stand out against darker terrain in the rendered trailing-side views, consistent with the near-full-phase Cassini reference.
dione.action: Retain the mapped fracture geography; use the visible monochrome reference for structure rather than inferring colour from mixed-filter imagery.
dione.limitations: The visualization texture has a slight colour cast and baked shading; neither is a calibrated material measurement. Canyons are visible in the image but are not explicitly modelled as 3D relief.

reference.title: Wispy Marble
reference.band: Cassini visible-light monochrome; near-full phase

references.title: Dione and Saturn
references.band: Archive-labelled natural-colour view; caption filter description inconsistent, not a calibration reference

dione.validation: Official archive image, source map and four rendered longitude views inspected; comparisons assess recognizable structure and colour class, not photometric equivalence.

rhea.name: Rhea
rhea.finding: The runtime surface remains grey and heavily cratered, consistent with the natural-colour left panel of the Cassini comparison. The enhanced blue/green right panel is not treated as visible colour.
rhea.action: Keep the restrained map colour and observed crater pattern.
rhea.limitations: Image contrast and scene exposure differ from the archive frame. Source shading is baked into the map, and fine-scale relief remains a texture feature.

reference.title: Color Across Rhea
reference.band: Left: RGB natural colour; right: enhanced ultraviolet/green/infrared

rhea.validation: Official archive image, source map and four rendered longitude views inspected; comparisons assess recognizable structure and colour class, not photometric equivalence.

titan.name: Titan
features: Surface hidden in ordinary visible light
titan.finding: The visible globe is smooth and gold, as in the Cassini RGB reference; no radar or infrared terrain is presented through the haze.
titan.action: Retain the opaque cloud reconstruction and subdued atmospheric limb.
titan.limitations: The haze map and limb scattering are approximations, not a dated weather reconstruction or a radiative-transfer model. Surface geography requires a separate non-visible observing mode.

reference.title: Titan in Natural Color
reference.band: Cassini red, green and blue natural colour

titan.validation: Official archive image, source map and four rendered longitude views inspected; comparisons assess recognizable structure and colour class, not photometric equivalence.

hyperion.name: Hyperion
hyperion.finding: The native mesh reproduces the irregular silhouette and crater-dominated structure. Its grey/olive display colour is less reddish than the natural appearance described by the Cassini archive caption.
hyperion.action: Keep the real source geometry and flag the colour uncertainty. Do not tune against the enhanced-colour reference as if it were calibrated RGB.
hyperion.limitations: The reference deliberately suppresses red and enhances other colours. The visualization texture includes baked shadows, and the mesh is not a calibrated elevation product.

reference.title: Saturn’s Battered Moon Hyperion
reference.band: Infrared, green and ultraviolet; red suppressed and other colours enhanced

hyperion.validation: Official archive image, source map and four rendered longitude views inspected; comparisons assess recognizable structure and colour class, not photometric equivalence.

iapetus.name: Iapetus
features: Equatorial ridge known from resolved Cassini images
iapetus.finding: The map reproduces the striking dark/bright contrast. The current ellipsoid does not reproduce the equatorial ridge silhouette; the inspected NASA visualization mesh is also effectively spherical and cannot supply that missing relief.
iapetus.action: Retain the observed albedo pattern and explicitly mark the absent ridge geometry instead of inventing a ridge.
iapetus.limitations: The comparison mosaic uses expanded wavelengths and exaggerates brown tones. Local terrain, including the ridge, is not resolved in the displayed shape.

reference.title: The Other Side of Iapetus
reference.band: Expanded-wavelength false-colour mosaic; browns exaggerated relative to natural colour

iapetus.validation: Official archive image, source map and four rendered longitude views inspected; comparisons assess recognizable structure and colour class, not photometric equivalence.

ariel.name: Ariel
ariel.finding: Mapped southern terrain contains the observed crater-and-valley pattern. The northern initial audit views expose extensive uniform fill because Voyager did not image that hemisphere in comparable detail.
ariel.action: Favor the photographed southern hemisphere when first focusing the moon; preserve unobserved areas as unspecified coverage rather than synthesizing terrain.
ariel.limitations: The clear-filter reference does not calibrate natural colour. Unmapped areas must not be interpreted as smooth real terrain; cliffs and canyon walls are not resolved in the ellipsoid.

reference.title: Ariel’s Densely Pitted Surface
reference.band: Voyager 2 clear-filter mosaic

ariel.validation: Official archive image, source map and four rendered longitude views inspected; comparisons assess recognizable structure and colour class, not photometric equivalence.

umbriel.name: Umbriel
umbriel.finding: The mapped hemisphere retains crater detail and the contrasting bright-ring feature. Northern views are predominantly uniform because photographic coverage is incomplete.
umbriel.action: Favor the observed southern hemisphere at initial focus while retaining an explicit coverage limitation.
umbriel.limitations: Uniform northern fill is unknown terrain, not an observation of a smooth surface. The visualization is not an absolute-reflectance calibration, and its geometry remains an ellipsoid.

reference.title: Umbriel
reference.band: Voyager 2 resolved southern-hemisphere observation

umbriel.validation: Official archive image, source map and four rendered longitude views inspected; comparisons assess recognizable structure and colour class, not photometric equivalence.

titania.name: Titania
titania.finding: The southern map carries the recognizable crater-and-fault pattern; the default northern audit views obscure much of it behind a uniform unobserved region.
titania.action: Start focused inspection toward the observed southern hemisphere and preserve missing coverage.
titania.limitations: The highest-resolution reference is a clear-filter mosaic, so the display map colour is not a measured true-colour result. Fault depth and northern terrain are not resolved.

reference.title: Titania - Highest Resolution Voyager Picture
reference.band: Voyager 2 clear-filter mosaic

titania.validation: Official archive image, source map and four rendered longitude views inspected; comparisons assess recognizable structure and colour class, not photometric equivalence.

oberon.name: Oberon
features: Dark material on some crater floors
Irregular relief visible at the photographed limb
oberon.finding: Mapped terrain preserves bright ray craters and darker crater floors. The northern uniform region hides much of the observed terrain from the initial northern audit angle.
oberon.action: Favor the observed southern terrain in the initial inspection view and retain the original coverage boundary.
oberon.limitations: Voyager colour uses violet, clear and green filters. The ellipsoid does not recreate individual limb mountains, and unmapped northern terrain is deliberately unspecified.

reference.title: Oberon at Voyager Closest Approach
reference.band: Voyager 2 violet, clear and green colour reconstruction

oberon.validation: Official archive image, source map and four rendered longitude views inspected; comparisons assess recognizable structure and colour class, not photometric equivalence.

miranda.name: Miranda
features: Angular banded coronae and chevron terrain
miranda.finding: The distinctive banded terrain exists in the southern map but is mostly hidden by the initial northern viewpoint, which shows a large featureless coverage fill.
miranda.action: Favor the photographed southern hemisphere for initial inspection without rotating or fabricating geographic data.
miranda.limitations: Voyager coverage is incomplete and partly monochrome. Dramatic scarps are represented in the texture, not explicit 3D cliff geometry; uniform fill is not known smooth terrain.

reference.title: Miranda - High Resolution Mosaic
reference.band: Voyager 2 clear-filter mosaic

miranda.validation: Official archive image, source map and four rendered longitude views inspected; comparisons assess recognizable structure and colour class, not photometric equivalence.

triton.name: Triton
triton.finding: The mapped southern terrain retains the major frost-cap and mottled surface patterns. A northern viewpoint shows extensive uniform fill outside the useful Voyager coverage.
triton.action: Favor the observed southern hemisphere when focusing, and keep the coverage gap visible rather than inventing the unobserved side.
triton.limitations: The reference assigns orange, violet and ultraviolet data to RGB and is not natural-colour calibration. Northern coverage is incomplete; the current texture is not a seasonally updated frost map.

reference.title: Global Color Mosaic of Triton
reference.band: Voyager 2 orange, violet and ultraviolet assigned to RGB; synthetic colour

triton.validation: Official archive image, source map and four rendered longitude views inspected; comparisons assess recognizable structure and colour class, not photometric equivalence.

janus.name: Janus

reference.title: Janus' Craters
reference.band: Visible-light monochrome; 272 m/pixel

features: Angular, irregular limb with broad depressions.
Large overlapping crater bowls and much finer cratering visible in the photograph.
One illuminated hemisphere; grayscale photograph cannot establish RGB color.
janus.finding: The previous smooth ellipsoid missed the characteristic outline and major depressions. Six runtime angles of the replacement show the measured broad crater forms. Small impacts in PIA14607 remain unresolved.
janus.action: Replace ellipsoid with Peter Thomas Cassini ISS PDS plate mesh (13,381 vertices, 26,758 triangles); use approximate neutral gray, no fabricated texture.
janus.limitations: PDS radii uncertain by 0.3-1.3 km, especially sub-Saturn. Small crater morphology is not reliable; no global albedo map was located. Shape-derived shading is not photographic small-scale terrain.

geometrySource.credit: Peter Thomas / Cassini ISS / NASA Planetary Data System

epimetheus.name: Epimetheus

reference.title: Examining Epimetheus
reference.band: Green polarized-light monochrome; 212 m/pixel

features: Irregular elongated outline and flattened southern region.
Soft-edged crater depressions with much smaller impacts in the photograph.
Green-filter polarized photograph is not a true-color view.
epimetheus.finding: The previous ellipsoid missed flattened and indented regions. Six runtime angles of the measured mesh recover the large-scale outline; fine photographic cratering remains absent.
epimetheus.action: Replace ellipsoid with Peter Thomas Cassini ISS PDS plate mesh (13,915 vertices, 27,826 triangles); preserve real major relief and approximate neutral gray.
epimetheus.limitations: PDS radii uncertain by 0.15-0.3 km, especially south pole. Small crater morphology is unreliable and no global photographic albedo map was located. Neutral tint is not calibrated RGB.

geometrySource.credit: Peter Thomas / Cassini ISS / NASA Planetary Data System

deimos.name: Deimos

reference.title: Deimos observed by HiRISE
reference.band: Enhanced color, not natural RGB

features: Rounded irregular outline, subdued small craters and smooth regolith.
Surface lacks the strong Phobos groove network.
HiRISE color is enhanced and cannot be copied as natural reflectance.
deimos.finding: The previous neutral ellipsoid omitted the observed irregular silhouette and markings. The native NASA model and six runtime views recover both, including smoother regolith regions.
deimos.action: Use original NASA GLB mesh and UV atlas (16,649 vertices, 32,512 triangles), retaining native UV orientation and a non-metallic surface.
deimos.limitations: NASA visualization mesh is not asserted to be a measured DTM. The texture preserves baked illumination, uneven coverage and some stretching; it cannot reproduce every HiRISE viewing angle.

amalthea.name: Amalthea

reference.title: Galileo's First Image of Amalthea
reference.band: Galileo SSI monochrome

features: Low-resolution Jupiter-facing end shows the broad Pan depression.
Bright south-polar Gaea feature; elongated shape is clearer in other Galileo viewing directions.
Fine terrain is unresolved in this photograph.
amalthea.finding: The previous ellipsoid omitted observed deviations from a smooth shape. The archival radial grid provides an elongated irregular body and broad depressions; uniform tint does not reproduce the bright Gaea patch.
amalthea.action: Import Philip Stooke NASA PDS Voyager radial grid at its original 5-degree sampling (2,522 vertices, 5,040 triangles). Keep approximate reddish tint and disclose missing albedo detail.
amalthea.limitations: Voyager-only model predates Galileo. PDS cautions Stooke depressions may be exaggerated and coordinates are offset from center of figure. Color and unresolved surface detail remain approximate.

geometrySource.credit: Philip Stooke / Voyager ISS / NASA Planetary Data System

phoebe.name: Phoebe

reference.title: Phoebe Cassini flyby mosaic
reference.band: Monochrome spacecraft mosaic; contrast enhanced

features: Irregular near-spherical silhouette and large deep impact basins.
Bright crater walls contrast with dark interiors; heavily cratered surface.
Photography and relative albedo both require exposure/coverage qualifications.
phoebe.finding: The previous neutral ellipsoid missed both large impact basins and real brightness variations. Six runtime views of the scientific DTM and registered relative-albedo map recover these features within documented coverage.
phoebe.action: Import 2023 Gaskell/Weirich NASA PDS shape, retaining every second original ICQ grid point; register the relative-albedo product in the source body frame. Mask author-marked suspect coverage to uniform gray.
phoebe.limitations: Source Q=128 grid is 1.195 km; retained display grid is about 2.39 km. Polar topography is less constrained. Relative albedo is not absolute reflectance; conservative coverage mask follows the author assessment, with about 53% of the cylindrical raster retained.

geometrySource.credit: Robert Gaskell / John Weirich et al. / Cassini ISS / NASA Planetary Data System

references.title: Phoebe SPC shape model quality assessment

larissa.name: Larissa

reference.title: Two Voyager 2 views of Larissa
reference.band: Voyager 2 monochrome

features: Only coarse irregular outline and large brightness patches are distinguishable.
No basis for a global finely cratered photographic surface.
larissa.finding: The smooth ellipsoid was too regular, but data do not justify a detailed global replacement. The archival low-resolution shape improves the observed side while remaining explicitly weakly constrained.
larissa.action: Use the original 5-degree NASA PDS Stooke grid, without adding detail. Identify the result as limited because the fit uses a single image.
larissa.limitations: PDS explicitly states the model is very poorly constrained and fit to only one image, primarily for estimating feature positions. The unseen side, albedo distribution and fine relief remain unknown.

geometrySource.credit: Philip Stooke / Voyager ISS / NASA Planetary Data System

proteus.name: Proteus

reference.title: Proteus observed by Voyager 2
reference.band: Voyager 2 monochrome; 8 km/pixel

features: Coarse box-like silhouette and broad depressions.
Voyager image has limited resolution and does not support high-frequency terrain.
proteus.finding: The smooth ellipsoid missed the box-like outline. The archival radial grid reproduces broad shape deviations visible across six runtime angles, without imaginary fine craters.
proteus.action: Use the original 5-degree NASA PDS Stooke grid and approximate neutral surface material; do not invent a global photographic map.
proteus.limitations: 5-degree Voyager grid gives broad shape only; archive cautions about faceting and exaggerated depression depths. No calibrated global visible albedo map is provided.

geometrySource.credit: Philip Stooke / Voyager ISS / NASA Planetary Data System

nereid.name: Nereid

reference.title: Nereid
reference.band: Voyager 2 monochrome; 43 km/pixel

features: Tiny pixelated disk with only gross brightness and outline information.
No resolved terrain pattern suitable for a surface texture.
nereid.finding: The archive does not resolve a reusable surface map or a detailed shape. Adding invented craters would reduce scientific fidelity.
nereid.action: Keep a plainly approximate smooth body and expose the official observation and unresolved-surface limitation.
nereid.limitations: Voyager reference resolves only 43 km per pixel at a distance of 4.7 million km. The displayed globe is a size-based approximation, not an observed detailed surface.
